analysis.evidence: וְהָיָה introduces the promised event. בְּעַנְנִי עָנָן עַל הָאָרֶץ gives its timing, “when I bring a cloud over the earth,” and וְנִרְאֲתָה הַקֶּשֶׁת בֶּעָנָן tells what will happen, “the bow will appear in the cloud.”
analysis.gloss: and it shall come to pass
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes the Qal perfect, third person masculine singular. In this promise, the form has future force and is used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: The following noun עָנָן supplies the cognate object and עַל הָאָרֶץ gives its location. Together the clause means “when I bring a cloud over the earth.”
analysis.morphology: The temporal preposition בְּ introduces a Piel infinitive construct. The first-person singular suffix marks the speaker as the subject of the infinitive.

analysis.evidence: In בְּעַנְנִי עָנָן עַל הָאָרֶץ, “when I bring a cloud over the earth,” עָנָן is the cognate object of בְּעַנְנִי. The verse then says that the bow appears בֶּעָנָן, “in the cloud.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine common noun, singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עָנָן עַל הָאָרֶץ places the cloud over the earth, and בֶּעָנָן locates the rainbow in that cloud. The phrase refers to the earth beneath the sky without singling out a territory.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes the common noun אֶרֶץ, singular absolute and of common gender. The definite form is הָאָרֶץ.
